chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman from our family has mixed [wealth] upon which zakat is due. He said: 'If it was worked with [i.e., used in trade/business], then zakat is upon her; and if it was not worked with, then no [zakat is due].'

key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: Zakat (alms-tax due on specific types of wealth)
key_terms.عُمِلَ بِهِ: It was worked with [used in trade/business]

ai.seo_question: When is zakat obligatory on mixed business capital in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between passive savings and active commercial capital, ruling that zakat is obligatory only when wealth is 'worked with' in trade. This establishes the principle of *amal* (employment/usage) as the trigger for liability, a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between *mal al-mustafad* (acquired wealth) and mere hoarding. The ruling underscores the economic spirit of zakat as a tax on productive capital rather than a static asset tax.
